sourcePolicy: Official ISM monthly reports are authoritative. This file stores a compact analytical snapshot and selected Power Stack-relevant observations, not a reconstructed ISM index database or confidential survey submissions.

manufacturing.powerStackInterpretation: Strongly supportive of the physical-infrastructure thesis. Production, orders and backlog accelerated while customer inventories fell further into 'too low' territory. Computer/electronics, machinery and electrical-equipment respondents described active AI/data-centre procurement ramps, semiconductor/connectivity demand and defence strength. The counterweight is still-hot input inflation and worsening delivery times, which favour suppliers with pricing power and backlog visibility over low-margin contractors.

services.powerStackInterpretation: Demand remains resilient, but inflation is not solved. Business activity and new orders accelerated while employment contracted and prices moved back above 70. Utility respondents reported persistent competition for electrical-equipment production slots; network gear lead times remain long. That supports grid, switchgear, cable and data-centre balance-of-system names, while high fuel/labour costs remain a margin risk for contractors and transport-intensive businesses.

combinedRead: July ISM is more bullish for Power Stack demand than for the broad economy: manufacturing re-accelerated sharply and services demand stayed firm, but both surveys still show physical bottlenecks and elevated prices. The best-positioned exposures remain grid equipment, electrical components, power generation, gas infrastructure and selected automation suppliers with pricing power and backlog visibility.
